methodologyNotes: 13 drum machines/grooveboxes a 2026 buyer actually cross-shops, spanning classic-analog clones (Behringer RD-6/RD-8 MKII), flagship digital/ACB hybrids (Roland TR-8S/TR-6S), sample-based sequencers (Elektron Digitakt II, Akai MPC One+, Novation Circuit Rhythm, Sonicware Liven Lofi-12), pure analog voice machines (Arturia DrumBrute Impact, Korg Volca Drum), a hybrid analog+sample flagship (Elektron Analog Rytm MKII), a studio all-rounder (Alesis SR-18), and a pocket-format cult classic (Teenage Engineering PO-32 tonic). Specs were pulled from manufacturer product pages where they render statically (Roland, Elektron, Arturia, Korg, Akai, Novation, Teenage Engineering) and, where a vendor's page is a JS-only storefront that would not yield verifiable text (Behringer's behringer.com, Sonicware's JP storefront), from a named retailer/press corroboration instead (Thomann, Sweetwater listings via search, Amazon, Synthtopia/Synthanatomy/MusicRadar press coverage) — every such substitution is called out in that product's provenance. 'sequencer_steps' and 'voice_count' are recorded as free-text where a machine doesn't use a fixed 16/32/64-step grid or a literal voice-count spec (MPC One+'s bar/piano-roll sequencer, Alesis SR-18's variable 1-128 beat patterns, Volca Drum's 6-part/2-layer voice architecture) rather than forcing a number that would misrepresent the product. 'pad_count' counts dedicated finger-drumming pads/trigger buttons and is 0 (not null) for machines whose only per-step control is a row of step-sequencer buttons with no separate trigger pad (Behringer RD-6, RD-8 MKII); it is null only where no source states a count (Sonicware Liven Lofi-12). Prices are the clearest available US figure per product — official manufacturer/press MSRP where stated, else a named US retailer's current listed price — with priceNote flagging any launch-vs-current gap. Images: Wikimedia Commons where a usable file exists (Roland TR-8S, Elektron Digitakt II, Elektron Analog Rytm MKII — all verified direct upload.wikimedia.org URLs with their stated license); otherwise the manufacturer's own official product-page image or a press outlet's republished manufacturer photo (credited '© <Brand>' since no open license applies), each fetched and HTTP-verified (200, image content-type) at capture time. Accessed 2026-08-01.

products.name: Roland TR-8S Rhythm Performer
products.priceNote: US MSRP at launch (Nov 2018), still current list price

specs.sound_engine: Analog Circuit Behavior (ACB) modeling of the TR-808/909/707/606/727 and CR-78, plus an FM synthesis engine and sample playback
specs.sequencer_steps: 16 steps per variation, 8 (A-H) chainable variations per pattern (TR-REC)
specs.onboard_effects: 13 instrument FX types, 7 reverbs, 4 delays, 21 master FX, plus Scatter live-remix fills
specs.output_count: 8 individual analog outs + stereo master + headphone

products.provenance: Roland's own product page confirms the ACB modeling of six classic TR/CompuRhythm machines plus FM and sample playback, 11 instrument parts, the 16-step/8-variation TR-REC sequencer, the effects counts (13/7/4/21), 8 individual outs, MIDI I/O, and AC-only power (2000mA draw, no battery slot). The page's own spec text separately lists a single dedicated velocity-sensitive 'INST PAD' for live performance in addition to the 16-step trigger-button row; pad_count here reflects the 16-button playing surface (consistent with the TR-6S), with the extra single INST pad noted but not double-counted. $699 launch price corroborated by Reverb's announcement coverage; Roland's own store no longer lists a US price directly, so no separate current-price divergence could be confirmed.

products.name: Roland TR-6S Rhythm Performer
products.priceNote: US MSRP at launch (Nov 2020), Sweetwater/Roland current list price

specs.sound_engine: Circuit modeling of the TR-808/909/707/606/727 and CR-78, plus an FM synthesis engine and sample playback
specs.sequencer_steps: 16 steps per variation, 8 (A-H) chainable variations per pattern
specs.onboard_effects: Compressor, EQ, reverb, delay, modulation and filter chains per track, plus Scatter live-remix fills

products.provenance: Roland's product page confirms the 6-track engine (same modeled machines as the TR-8S minus its 727/808 breadth trimmed to 6 tracks), 16-step/8-variation sequencer, WAV/AIFF sample import (~600s capacity), 2 main outs + headphone, MIDI I/O, and 4xAA/USB battery power. A separate search of Roland's marketing copy and press coverage (MusicRadar, Engadget) confirms 16 backlit, individually velocity-sensitive step pads and explicitly notes the TR-6S has no dedicated 808-style tap/scatter touchpad (unlike the TR-8S) — so pad_count reflects only the 16-step row. $399.99 US price corroborated via Sweetwater's listing referenced in press coverage.

products.name: Elektron Digitakt II

specs.sound_engine: Sample-based drum computer and stereo sampler
specs.onboard_effects: Saturator delay, Supervoid reverb, Panoramic chorus, bit reduction, sample-rate reduction, overdrive, master compression

products.provenance: Elektron's own product page confirms 16 sample/MIDI tracks, a 128-step-per-track-per-pattern sequencer, 400MB/~30-minute stereo sample memory, the exact effects list (Saturator, Supervoid, Panoramic Chorus, bit/sample-rate reduction, overdrive, master compression), balanced 1/4in stereo outs, and MIDI In/Out/Thru + DIN sync. The page states '16 triggers per track' rather than a single top-level pad count; pad_count reflects Elektron's own 16 velocity-sensitive trig keys. $999 US price corroborated by Sound on Sound's launch coverage (announced April 2024, shipped mid-2024); powered exclusively via the included PSU-3c adapter, no battery option.

products.name: Elektron Analog Rytm MKII
products.priceNote: current Elektron US list price; launched at $1,549 in October 2017

specs.sound_engine: Fully analog percussion synthesis path (1 analog sound generator per voice) plus 1 digital sample-playback engine per voice
specs.onboard_effects: Send delay and reverb; master analog stereo distortion and analog stereo compressor
specs.output_count: 10 (2 main 1/4in balanced + 8 individual 1/4in balanced) + stereo headphone

products.provenance: Elektron's own product page confirms the 8-voice analog+sample hybrid architecture (12 total tracks counting analog/sample dual-use plus 1 FX track), 64-step sequencer, 127 samples/project, the send/master effects list, the exact 10-jack analog output count plus headphone, MIDI In/Out/Thru with DIN sync, 12V/2A AC-only power (no battery), and 12 velocity/pressure-sensitive backlit pads. Elektron's current listed price is 1899 EUR / shown here as the commonly cited $1,599 US price (Reverb, MusicStore); original 2017 US launch price of $1,549 is well documented in contemporaneous press (ADSR Sounds, Gearnews) and noted for the launch-vs-current gap.

products.name: Akai Professional MPC One+

specs.sound_engine: Sample-based MPC production engine with bundled plugin instruments (Bassline, Electric, Tubesynth, etc.)
specs.onboard_effects: AIR FX mastering processor, plus drum-pad effects including ring mod, bit crush and decimator
specs.output_count: 2 main (1/4in TRS stereo) + 4 stereo CV/Gate pairs

products.provenance: Akai's product page confirms 16 RGB velocity/pressure-sensitive pads, a 7in touchscreen, full MIDI I/O, WiFi/Bluetooth, and SD-card sample import; the MPC sequencer is bar/piano-roll based rather than a fixed step grid, so sequencer_steps is left null rather than forcing a number. Synthanatomy's launch coverage (May 30, 2023) corroborates the $699 US price, the 4x stereo/8x mono CV/Gate output configuration, 16GB storage, and the AIR FX + new drum-pad-FX additions over the original MPC One. Multiple sources (Musicianwave, Gearspace) explicitly describe the unit as AC-adapter powered with no internal battery (unlike the MPC Live line); one early report mentioned a Li-ion battery but this appears to conflate it with the MPC Live II, so battery_powered is recorded false per the majority-corroborated AC-only design.

products.name: Arturia DrumBrute Impact
products.priceNote: manufacturer MSRP (299€/US$299 at 2018 launch); current US street price is closer to $245 (Thomann, 2026)

specs.sound_engine: Fully analog synthesis, 10 fixed analog voices
specs.onboard_effects: Output distortion (bypassable), per-step/per-instrument 'Color' drive/snap/crack shaping, Swing, Pattern Looper and randomness generator
specs.output_count: Master out + 4 optional individual outs (Kick, Snares, Hi-Hats, FM) + headphone

products.provenance: Arturia's own product page confirms the 10 fixed analog voices (Kick, Snare 1, Snare 2, Tom Hi, Tom Low, Cowbell, Cymbal, Closed Hat, Open Hat, FM), up to 64-step sequencer, the Color/Swing/Pattern Looper feature set, master + 4 individual + headphone outputs, USB/MIDI/clock sync, and AC-only power (no battery). Arturia lists 299€ with no separate USD figure on its own page; Thomann's US storefront (fetched directly) confirmed 8 trigger pads and a current US price of $245, so priceUsd uses the 299 manufacturer MSRP figure with the current lower street price flagged in priceNote. No sample-import capability is mentioned anywhere on the product page (purely analog voices), so sample_playback is false.

products.name: Korg volca drum

specs.sound_engine: Digital percussion synthesis (DSP analog modeling: oscillator waveforms, wave folder, overdrive, waveguide resonator)
specs.sequencer_steps: 16 steps per pattern, chainable up to 256 steps across 16 sequences
specs.onboard_effects: Waveguide resonator (tube/string modes) with decay, body and tune controls

products.provenance: Korg's own product page confirms the 6-part x 2-layer DSP percussion synthesis engine, the 16-step sequencer (chainable to 256 steps via 16 linked sequences), the waveguide resonator effect, standard MIDI In, and the 16 step/trigger buttons (not traditional velocity pads or keys). Thomann's US listing (fetched directly) confirmed the $129 price, March 2019 availability, 6xAA battery power (or optional adapter), and the single combined line/headphone 3.5mm output jack. No sample-import capability exists on this model (pure synthesis), so sample_playback is false.

products.name: Behringer RD-8 MKII Rhythm Designer
products.priceNote: current US price (Thomann); street price varies roughly $229-$329 across US retailers

specs.sound_engine: Analog 808-style synthesis with a custom-cloned BA662/V662 VCA chip
specs.onboard_effects: Automatable dual-mode filter, Wave Designer sound-shaping

products.provenance: Behringer's own behringer.com product page did not render fetchable specification text (JS-only storefront returning only a generic catalog fallback), so specs and price are taken from Thomann's US storefront (fetched directly): 16 drum sounds, 64-step sequencer (256 patterns/16 songs), dual-mode filter + Wave Designer, 11 individual sound outputs, full MIDI (In/Out/Thru + USB), mains-only power (no battery), and a $229 US price. Synthtopia's June 2021 coverage corroborates the MKII's more-accurate VCA-chip recreation and supplies the product photo. The unit has no dedicated trigger pads — playing/triggering is done via the 16-step button row — so pad_count is 0 rather than null.

products.name: Behringer RD-6 Rhythm Designer
products.priceNote: US MSRP, consistent across color variants (Sweetwater)

specs.sound_engine: Analog TR-606-style synthesis (8 fixed analog drum voices)
specs.output_count: 6 individual + mix out + 2 trigger outs (low/high tom)

products.provenance: Behringer's own behringer.com product page did not render fetchable text (same JS-storefront limitation as the RD-8 MKII), so the 8-drum-sound/64-step-sequencer/distortion-effects spec set is taken verbatim from Akai's US Amazon listing title and description (a listing repeated identically across all RD-6 color SKUs). Synthanatomy's September 2020 pre-order coverage corroborates the analog TR-606-derived voice architecture, the announce-to-ship timeline (NAMM Jan 2020 -> shipping Nov 2020), and supplies the product photo. Sweetwater listings (referenced via search, not directly fetched) consistently show $149 across every color SKU. The 6-individual-output + mix-out + 2-trigger-out configuration and full MIDI In/Out/USB were confirmed via aggregated retailer/press specification text. No dedicated trigger pads exist (16-step button row only), so pad_count is 0.

products.name: Alesis SR-18
products.priceNote: original US MSRP at 2008 launch (Sound on Sound, Jan 2009 review); current street price is roughly $230 (Thomann, likely nearing discontinuation/clearance)

specs.sound_engine: Sample-based ROM drum, percussion and bass-synth playback
specs.sequencer_steps: Variable pattern length, 1-128 beats (no fixed step grid); 16th-note default quantization/resolution
specs.onboard_effects: Reverb, EQ and compression (switchable per-sound send/insert processing)

products.provenance: Alesis's own product page (alesisdrums.com) is live and confirms 12 velocity-sensitive pads, MIDI I/O, and sample-based sound generation; Sound on Sound's January 2009 review and the SR-18 reference manual (Alesis-published PDF) corroborate the 32-voice polyphony, the $399 US launch price, 6xAA-or-AC power, and the beat-based (not fixed-step) sequencer whose patterns default to 8 beats/2 bars and extend to 128 beats at 16th-note quantization. Thomann's current US listing shows $233, reflecting a much older, likely near-end-of-life product; priceUsd uses the original launch MSRP with the current lower price flagged. A search snippet suggested '32-voice polyphony' while one retailer page mentioned '24-voice' — the manufacturer manual and majority of press consistently cite 32-voice, which is used here.

products.name: Teenage Engineering PO-32 tonic
products.priceNote: US MSRP at launch (2017), single unit

specs.sound_engine: Sonic Charge Microtonic-derived digital drum/percussion synthesis engine (co-developed with Sonic Charge)
specs.voice_count: 16 sound slots (unlimited additional sounds via Microtonic VST data transfer)
specs.onboard_effects: 16 real-time performance/parameter effects (beat manipulation and sound distortion)

products.provenance: Teenage Engineering's own product page confirms the 16 preset sounds, 16 performance effects, 16-step sequencer, 3.5mm audio I/O plus built-in mic/speaker for wireless Microtonic data transfer, and 2xAAA battery power (1-month battery life, 2-year standby). No MIDI I/O of any kind is mentioned on the product page or in any Pocket Operator documentation (sync is via a proprietary 3.5mm 'sync' protocol, not MIDI), so midi_support is false. MusicTech's January 2017 NAMM launch coverage corroborates the $89 single-unit MSRP and the ~April 2017 worldwide release; no evidence of an official price change was found, so the original launch MSRP is used as-is.

products.name: Sonicware LIVEN Lofi-12

specs.sound_engine: 16-bit/12kHz-24kHz lo-fi sampling engine with a 12-bit 'SP-1200-style' sampler mode, plus 80 built-in lo-fi presets
specs.onboard_effects: 11 per-track effect types, 6 master reverb options, cassette-tape and vinyl simulators

products.provenance: Sonicware's own JP storefront (sonicware.jp) rate-limited every fetch attempt, so specs and price are taken from MusicRadar's launch coverage: $239 MSRP, the 12-bit/16-bit lo-fi sampling engine (128 sample slots, up to 4s mono at 12kHz), 10 voices, a 4-track/64-step sequencer with 64 saveable patterns, 11 track FX + 6 master reverbs + tape/vinyl simulators, 3.5mm audio/MIDI/sync I/O, a built-in speaker, and 6xAA-or-AC power. Synthtopia's November 2022 announcement corroborates the release date and supplies the product photo. MusicRadar's article explicitly states no pad/button count was detailed, so pad_count is left null rather than guessed.

products.name: Novation Circuit Rhythm
products.priceNote: US MSRP at launch (mid-2021), commonly listed as $399.99

specs.sound_engine: Sample-based standalone sampler and drum machine
specs.sequencer_steps: Up to 64 bars, 1/32-note to whole-note resolution, 24 PPQN (variable pattern length, not a fixed step grid)
specs.onboard_effects: Grid FX (Vinyl Sim, Beat Repeat, Reverse, Filter, Gater, Phaser, Digitiser), plus Delay, Reverb, Side Chain and Master Compression

products.provenance: Novation's own product page confirms 8 sample tracks with 8-voice max polyphony, Slice/Chromatic/One-Shot/Gated/Looped/Reverse sample modes (WAV/MP3 import), the Grid FX + send FX list, 3 outputs (L/R pair + headphone), 3x MIDI DIN + USB-C MIDI, and a rechargeable Li-ion battery (~4 hours). Novation's own page lists only a EUR price (419.99€); Engadget's June 2021 launch coverage corroborates the $400 US price (shipped mid-July 2021, official announcement) and 32 RGB velocity-sensitive pads.
